lines.trans: Where did the two of you meet?
He was an upperclassman's friend, and we were introduced at a campus festival.
How long did you go out with that boyfriend?
About three months, I think.
What happened? Did you end up breaking up?
My boyfriend was way too controlling, so I got fed up with it.
Welcome home. Don't say it's cramped—it's a lovely room.
Somehow this feels so fun. I'll gladly clean the bathroom too.
We'll have to set rules for shower turns and doing the laundry.
And let's take turns cooking meals. If something tastes bad, let's tell each other honestly.
This place right here is plenty fine for me.
From now on, let's both do what we love and live freely.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for place.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 先輩の先輩で、学園祭に行った時に紹介されまして。
examples.trans: He was an upperclassman's friend, and we were introduced at a campus festival.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

examples.text: 私何か悪いことした？あんた私の彼氏？
examples.trans: Did I do something wrong? What are you, my boyfriend?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Interrogative prenoun adjectival; どのぐらい means 'about how much/many'.

examples.text: どのぐらいかかりますか。
examples.trans: About how long does it take?

examples.text: 三カ月ぐらいかと思います。
現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to quantities or interrogatives (どのぐらい, 何本ぐらい) to indicate approximation.

examples.text: 一日何本ぐらい売れる？
examples.trans: About how many sell in a day?

examples.text: 十分ぐらい待ちました。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Colloquial particle, often used to downplay or dismiss.

examples.text: テレビなんか見ていないで勉強しろ。
コーヒーなんかどうですか。
examples.trans: How about some coffee or something?

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: なんか彼氏があんまり束縛するんで、イヤになっちゃって。
examples.trans: My boyfriend was way too controlling, so I got fed up with it.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: おはようございます。皆さんステキですわ。
examples.trans: Good morning. You all look wonderful.

examples.text: ホントにステキなセンスですね。どうしてお仕事お辞めになられたんですか？
examples.trans: You truly have lovely taste. Why did you leave your job?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

examples.text: なんだか楽しいですわね。トイレのお掃除とかもやりますわよ。
examples.trans: Somehow this feels so fun. I'll gladly clean the bathroom too.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.

examples.text: 下手するとお前も掃除されるぞ。
examples.trans: Make one misstep and you will get swept away yourself.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

examples.text: 遅い！シャワーを浴びてこい、二分後に撮影するぞ。
examples.trans: Too slow! Go take a shower, we roll in two minutes.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: シャワーの順番とか洗濯のルールとか決めないとね。
examples.trans: We'll have to set rules for shower turns and doing the laundry.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; potential form 決められる means 'can decide'.

examples.text: まだ何も決めていません。
今決められないなら、後で考えましょう。
examples.trans: If you can't decide now, let's think about it later.

examples.text: あとごはんは当番制でいっか。まずかったらちゃんと言い合おうね。
examples.trans: And let's take turns cooking meals. If something tastes bad, let's tell each other honestly.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.note: Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。
あとごはんは当番制でいっか。まずかったらちゃんと言い合おうね。
examples.trans: And let's take turns cooking meals. If something tastes bad, let's tell each other honestly.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

examples.text: お互いにとってタイミングが合ってよかったって。
examples.trans: She says she's glad the timing worked out for both of you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Na-adjective; the thing liked is marked with が or は.

examples.text: どんな食べ物が好きですか。
examples.trans: What kind of food do you like?

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Ichidan verb.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
